title: U.S. House · Georgia's 8th District
area: South-central Georgia, including Warner Robins, Tifton, Moultrie, and Valdosta.

context.text: Cook Political Report rates this race Solid Republican; Decision Desk, Inside Elections, and Sabato's Crystal Ball also rate it Safe/Solid Republican.

Roman Coley Davis (Independent), whom Ballotpedia lists as withdrawn or disqualified, does not appear on the printed U.S. House District 8 contest on the Houston County Nov. 3, 2026 sample ballot, which lists Austin Scott and Kelly Esti with a write-in line.

candidates.name: Austin Scott
candidates.ballotNote: Won the May 19 Republican primary unopposed on the ballot after Vinson Watkins withdrew

summary.text: Austin Scott has represented Georgia's 8th Congressional District since 2011 and is now in his eighth term. He previously served in the Georgia House of Representatives and owned an insurance brokerage firm for nearly 20 years before being elected to Congress. He is Vice Chairman of the House Agriculture Committee.

background.text: Earned a B.B.A. in risk management and insurance from the University of Georgia (1993, according to Ballotpedia).
Owned and operated an insurance brokerage firm for nearly 20 years before running for Congress.
Served in the Georgia House of Representatives from 1997 to 2010, according to Ballotpedia.

Elected to the U.S. House on November 2, 2010, defeating incumbent Rep. Jim Marshall (D) with 52.7% of the vote; took office in 2011 and has been re-elected since, most recently advancing from the unopposed May 19, 2026 Republican primary.

In the 119th Congress (2025-2026), serves as Vice Chairman of the House Committee on Agriculture and Chair of its General Farm Commodities, Risk Management, and Credit Subcommittee; also sits on the Rules Committee, the Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence, and the Armed Services Committee.
Co-chairs the Congressional Crop Insurance Caucus and, according to his official biography, serves on the Board of Visitors for the Western Hemisphere Institute for Security Cooperation.

Ballotpedia lists memberships in the American Red Cross Coastal Plains Chapter Board, the National Association of Insurance Financial Advisers, First Baptist Church of Tifton, and the American Legislative Exchange Council. His official biography says he and his wife Vivien live in Tifton and have three children.

priorities.text: Says he is proud to be pro-life and remains fully committed to the belief that life begins at conception, and to protecting the lives of the unborn.

Says reducing federal spending and working toward a balanced budget has been one of his top priorities since coming to Congress, citing the national debt as one of the greatest threats to the country's economic security.

As a member of the House Committee on Agriculture, says he works to advocate on behalf of Georgia's ranchers and farmers and to help author a Farm Bill that benefits the state's agricultural community.

positions.summary: His official site says he is pro-life, believes life begins at conception, and has voted for and cosponsored numerous bills restricting abortion and defunding Planned Parenthood.
positions.quote: I am proud to be pro-life and am committed to protecting the lives of the unborn. I believe that life begins at conception, and developments in science continue to confirm that truth.

positions.summary: His official site says he opposes adding layers of gun control, saying such measures would do little to protect citizens, and pledges to continue supporting and protecting Second Amendment rights.
positions.quote: We can fight crime by holding criminals accountable for their actions, not by disregarding the Second Amendment of the U.S. Constitution and adding layers of gun control that would do little to nothing to protect our citizens.

positions.summary: His official site says the country must secure its borders, remove illegal immigrants currently in the country, and enforce existing immigration laws before any reform is considered.
positions.quote: We must first secure our borders, remove the illegal immigrants currently in our country and enforce our existing immigration laws before we attempt to implement any type of immigration reform.

positions.summary: His official site says he opposed the Affordable Care Act as a government takeover of health care and voted to repeal it, favoring market-based reforms instead.
positions.quote: I co-sponsored and voted for H.R. 2 to repeal the Patient Protection and Affordable Care Act.

positions.summary: His official site says ensuring Israel's continued qualitative military edge and completing the U.S.-Israel 10-year Memorandum of Understanding for military assistance is a key national security priority.
positions.quote: I believe that ensuring Israel's continued qualitative military edge in the region and completing the U.S.-Israel 10-year Memorandum of Understanding for military assistance remains a key American national security priority.

record.text: Serves as Vice Chair of the House Committee on Agriculture and Chair of its General Farm Commodities, Risk Management, and Credit Subcommittee in the 119th Congress (2025-2026).
Voted for and cosponsored H.R. 3134, the Defund Planned Parenthood Act, and H.R. 217, the Title X Abortion Provider Prohibition Act, among other abortion-related bills listed on his official site.

candidates.name: Kelly Esti
candidates.ballotNote: Won the May 19 Democratic primary, defeating Justin Lucas

summary.text: Kelly Esti is the Democratic nominee for Georgia's 8th Congressional District. A U.S. Navy veteran, he describes himself as an entrepreneur, scholar, and advocate, works as an analyst with Delta Air Lines, and has held local board roles in the Atlanta area. He is running on community engagement, lower costs, education and transportation.

background.text: According to Ballotpedia, he earned a high school diploma from South Pike High School.
Served in the U.S. Navy from 1999 to 2002, according to Ballotpedia; in his own words he enlisted after high school as a nuclear-trained sailor.

Holds a bachelor's degree from Ottawa University, a graduate degree from Webster University, and a Ph.D. from Walden University per Ballotpedia; he describes his degrees as a Ph.D. in public policy, an MBA with a focus in finance, and a B.A. in management.
Says he has worked with JPMorganChase, E*Trade Financial, and UPS, and currently works as an analyst with Delta Air Lines.

Says he served on the Fulton County Zoning Board, as a board member and School Performance and Academic Chair for the Main Street Academy charter school, as a Hapeville Board of Appeals member, and as Legislative Chair for Georgia Equality.
Describes himself as one of the founders of the city of South Fulton, Georgia.
Won the May 19, 2026 Democratic primary over Justin Lucas, 53.5% to 46.5%.

priorities.text: Says he will commit to regular town halls and to making his congressional office "a place where citizens can come learn and be empowered through knowledge."
Wants to ensure wealthy individuals and large multinational corporations "pay their fair share of taxes" to fund infrastructure, rural broadband, education, and lower healthcare costs.
Proposes a Georgia intercity rail system ("the Georgia Intrastate Transit") connecting the state's large cities to reduce road wear, congestion, and pollution.

Campaign website lists policy priorities in military and veterans services, education, utilities and renewable energy, healthcare, infrastructure (roads, broadband, transit), worker rights and civil rights.

statements.quote: As your congressman, my role is to strengthen federal health programs, support funding for rural clinics and hospitals, and work with agencies to improve access to essential services throughout the district.
statements.context: On his campaign website's Healthcare page

statements.quote: As renewable energy, like solar and wind, becomes more affordable nationwide, communities should have the option to explore these alternatives if they believe they will reduce long-term costs.
statements.context: On his campaign website's Utilities & Renewable Energy page

statements.quote: ensuring wealthy individuals and large multinational corporations pay their fair share of taxes to fund investments in infrastructure, digital expansion like fiber internet into rural areas, education
statements.context: In his 2026 Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey

candidates.researchNotes: Campaign website (kellyesti4congress.com) has issue pages written in general terms; no explicit stance on abortion, guns, immigration, or tariffs was found.

researchNotes: Basic-tier research from Ballotpedia. Roman Coley Davis has little public footprint beyond his Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey answers; no campaign website was located. Roman Coley Davis (Independent), listed by Ballotpedia as withdrawn or disqualified, does not appear on the printed U.S. House District 8 contest of the Houston County Nov. 3, 2026 sample ballot (only Austin Scott and Kelly Esti plus write-in line), so he has no entry here. Biography update: Ballotpedia states Roman Coley Davis will not appear on the November 3, 2026 general election ballot and lists him as withdrawn or disqualified; his entry may need to be removed, and no biographical details beyond his survey answers were found.
